family_lesson.where_to_look_first: Break or scratch a noncritical tissue only when appropriate and observe the latex, then inspect the flower base and fruit: 2–3 quickly falling sepals, free showy petals, many free stamens, and a superior syncarpous capsule are the core sequence.
core_characters: Mostly herbs; sap/latex commonly white, yellow, orange or watery.
Leaves usually alternate and without stipules; often lobed or divided.
Sepals commonly 2–3 and caducous, falling as the flower opens.
Petals commonly 4–6, free, often crumpled or pleated in bud.
Ovary superior, syncarpous, usually 1-locular with parietal placentation.
Fruit usually a capsule dehiscing by valves or pores.
local_argemone_pattern: Glaucous, prickly annual/biennial herbs with colored latex.
Argemone typically has 2–3 horned, caducous sepals, commonly 6 petals, numerous stamens and a prickly capsule.
Capsule-prickle architecture is more useful than petal color for species separation.

Ranunculaceae.confusion: Both can have many free stamens and showy flowers.
Ranunculaceae.tie_breaker: Papaveraceae has syncarpous capsule + parietal placentation + caducous 2–3 sepals + latex; Ranunculaceae more often has several free carpels/aggregate fruits.

Malvaceae.confusion: Many stamens can dominate the flower center.
Malvaceae.tie_breaker: Malvaceae commonly organizes stamens into a staminal column/tube; Papaveraceae stamens are generally free and surrounds a syncarpous capsule-forming ovary.

cards.look_here_first: Ignore the white petals. Inspect the capsule prickles: the longest are very unequal and commonly branched, reaching roughly 15–35 mm in Flora of North America descriptions.
confirm: Accepted Texas endemic species under current POWO.
Annual/biennial with prickly stems and deeply lobed prickly leaves.
Capsule ovoid with very unequal herbaceous prickles; longest often branched and 15–35 mm.
Original species description identifies red-orange latex; use latex as supporting evidence, not the only character.
cards.tie_breaker: A. aurantiaca: branched, very long unequal capsule prickles. A. albiflora: capsule prickles generally much shorter/simple in FNA keying; local A. albiflora subsp. texana descriptions also show a different mixed but shorter fruit-prickle architecture.

cards.look_here_first: Inspect the flower bud/sepals and capsule rather than relying on white petals. In the FNA key, A. albiflora falls with simple shorter capsule prickles rather than the very long branched prickles of A. aurantiaca.
confirm: Current POWO recognizes subsp. albiflora and subsp. texana.
UT's detailed Texas treatment of the taxon called A. albiflora var. texana corresponds nomenclaturally to accepted A. albiflora subsp. texana.
Detailed Texas material has light-yellow latex, glaucous stems/leaves, caducous horned sepals, hundreds of stamens and a prickly capsule.
cards.taxonomy_note: Do not automatically convert every Texas/Hays A. albiflora record to subsp. texana. The Master Pool remains species-level until the observation/source specimens are reviewed under the accepted infraspecific treatment.
